Abstract
               
                  Motivation
                  Tracking disease outbreaks by whole-genome sequencing leads to the collection of large samples of closely related sequences. Five years ago, we published a method to accurately compute all pairwise distances for such samples by indexing each sequence. Since indexing is slow, we now ask whether it is possible to achieve similar accuracy when indexing only a single sequence.
               
               
                  Results
                  We have implemented this idea in the program phylonium and show that it is as accurate as its predecessor and roughly 100 times faster when applied to all 2678 Escherichia coli genomes contained in ENSEMBL. One of the best published programs for rapidly computing pairwise distances, mash, analyzes the same dataset four times faster but, with default settings, it is less accurate than phylonium.
               
               
                  Availability and implementation
                  Phylonium runs under the UNIX command line; its C++ sources and documentation are available from github.com/evolbioinf/phylonium.
               
               
                  Supplementary information
                  Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

result.paraphrase:
Abstract

Motivation
Whole-genome sequencing for outbreak tracking produces large sets of closely related sequences. Five years earlier, we introduced a method that accurately computes all pairwise distances in such datasets by indexing every sequence. Because indexing is time-consuming, we now examine whether similar accuracy can be achieved by indexing just one sequence.

Results
We implemented this approach in phylonium and demonstrate that it matches the accuracy of its predecessor while running about 100 times faster on the 2678 Escherichia coli genomes in ENSEMBL. Mash, one of the strongest published tools for rapid pairwise distance calculation, processes the same dataset four times faster but is less accurate than phylonium with default settings.

Availability and implementation
Phylonium runs from the UNIX command line, and its C++ source code and documentation are available at github.com/evolbioinf/phylonium.

Supplementary information
Supplementary data are available online at Bioinformatics.
